parts.title: Learning to climb
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I never thought that I would enjoy climbing. I am afraid of heights, and when my friend Tomas invited me to try the indoor wall at the sports centre, I almost said no. But he promised that the ropes were safe, so I agreed.

The first ten minutes were terrible. My hands shook, and I could not look down. Then the instructor, a calm woman called Reena, told me to stop thinking about the top and just look for the next hold. It was really good advice. By the end of the lesson, I had reached the roof of the wall, and I was smiling.

Since then, I have been going every Saturday. I have learned that climbing is as much about thinking as it is about strength, because you have to plan every move. I have also made new friends at the wall, and we often have coffee together afterwards.

Last month, Tomas and I climbed a real rock outside for the first time. It was much harder than the wall, and my legs ached for two days. But the view from the top made it worth it.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer agree to try climbing?
options: He was not afraid of heights
He wanted to meet new people
His friend said it was safe
questions.explanation: Tomas promised that the ropes were safe, so he agreed.

questions.explanation: Reena told him to stop thinking about the top and look for the next hold.

questions.prompt: What has the writer learned about climbing?
options: It is easier for tall people

It is dangerous without a partner
questions.explanation: Climbing is as much about thinking as about strength, because you plan every move.

questions.prompt: What do the climbers often do afterwards?
questions.explanation: They often have coffee together afterwards.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel about the outdoor climb?
options: It was too windy to enjoy
It was easier than the wall
questions.explanation: It was much harder, but the view made it worth it.

parts.title: A weekend on the mountain
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
We left the car park at seven o'clock on Saturday morning, with heavy rucksacks and high hopes. [1] The path was steep, and after an hour my brother had already asked three times if we were nearly there.

By midday, we had reached a small lake. [2] We sat on a flat rock and ate our sandwiches while a few sheep watched us. The air was fresh and quiet, and I felt very far from the city.

In the afternoon, clouds began to gather. [3] Our guide, Mr Orsini, decided that we should go down to a hut instead of continuing to the top. I was disappointed, but he reminded us that mountains are dangerous in bad weather. [4] When we arrived, the hut owner gave us hot soup, and it was the best meal I have ever had.

The next morning, the sky was clear, and we climbed to the summit in two hours. [5] I took a photograph, but it can never show how amazing it felt.
sentences: We reached the hut just before the rain started.
It was the perfect place to stop for lunch.
A helicopter flew over us while we were eating.
For the first hour, we walked through a forest of tall pine trees.
My brother wants to become a mountain guide.
The view from the top was bigger than I had imagined.
It was clear that the weather was going to change.
Mr Orsini has climbed this mountain more than a hundred times.

gaps.explanation: The forest walk describes the first part, and "the path was steep" continues the description.
"Perfect place to stop" explains why they sat down and ate their sandwiches.
The gathering clouds lead to "the weather was going to change", then the guide's decision.
They reached the hut, and "when we arrived" refers to this arrival, just before the rain.
The summit is the top, and the sentence describes the view from there.

We saw some goats [4] were standing on the edge of a cliff. Tomorrow, we plan to go [5] foot to a waterfall. I wish you [6] here with us!

parts.title: Mountain safety tips

parts.passage: Before you go walking in the mountains, check the weather forecast. Wear strong boots [1] cover your ankles, and take a waterproof jacket [2] case it rains. Always tell someone [3] you are going and when you expect to return. Take plenty of water [4] food. If the weather gets worse, do not [5] on; turn back. Remember that it is better to arrive late [6] not to arrive at all.

We tell someone the place that we are going to.
Water and food are two things to take.

turns.text: Good morning, visitors. This is a message from the cable car station. Some of you may know that the last cable car down usually leaves at half past five in the evening. parts.title: A day walk
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: tania
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Highpoint Adventure Centre. My name is Tania, and I’ll be your guide today. We’re going on a day walk to Eagle Rock. The brochure says it’s twelve kilometres, but that is the long route. Today we’re doing the standard one, which is ten kilometres. It takes about five hours, including a lunch stop. Some people say four, but we walk slowly and take photos. We start at nine from the front of the centre, so please be ready by ten to. Now, equipment. Many of you are wearing trainers, and I’m sorry, but they’re not good on wet rocks. Everyone must wear strong boots. If you don’t have them, you can hire a pair at the desk for three pounds. A waterproof coat is also important, though I hope we won’t need it. Now, food and drink. Take lunch in your rucksack, and each person needs one litre of water. Some people carry two, and that’s fine, but it’s heavy, and we have a stop at a stream where you can fill your bottle. About the weather. The forecast is good, but mountains change quickly. If it turns bad, we won’t go to the top. We’ll take the shorter path along the river and have lunch in the hut. It’s less beautiful, but safer. One last thing. The day costs thirty pounds. The fee includes a map of the area that you can keep, and a hot drink at the hut. Lunch is not included, so please bring your own. Does anyone have any questions before we leave? Good, then follow me.

gaps.explanation: The brochure says twelve, but that is the long route; today’s route is ten.

gaps.prompt: Allow about ___ hours for the walk
gaps.explanation: Some people say four, but they walk slowly and stop for lunch, so it takes about five hours.

gaps.prompt: Walkers must have suitable ___ for wet rocks
gaps.explanation: Trainers are not good on wet rocks; everyone must wear strong boots.

gaps.prompt: Each person should carry one ___ of water
gaps.explanation: Some people carry two, but one litre is enough because there is a stream.

gaps.prompt: If the weather is bad, the group follows the ___ route
gaps.explanation: They will not go to the top; they take the shorter path along the river.

gaps.prompt: The fee includes a ___ of the area
gaps.explanation: The fee covers a map and a hot drink; lunch is not included.

parts.title: A mountain guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: Gethin, you’ve guided people for twenty years. What made you start climbing?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: I’d love to say it was a film, and I did see a famous one at university, but I’d been climbing for years by then. And nobody offered me a job after school. I just had a rucksack and an old map. It was a school trip when I was seven. Our teacher took us up a small hill in Wales, and I thought I had reached the top of the world.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: What do you do first on a working day?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: Before I phone my clients or pack the ropes, I check the weather. Always. I look at three different websites, and then I look at the sky. The mountain doesn’t care about our plans, so the plan must change if the weather changes.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: What is the most dangerous thing for you?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: Everyone expects me to say wild animals, but I’ve never had a problem with them. Heavy rucksacks hurt your back, but that isn’t dangerous. Thick fog is the real problem. You can’t see the path or the edge, and people panic. It can take just a minute to lose the group.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: What mistakes do your clients make?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: They’re very enthusiastic, and they certainly don’t start too early, that’s the opposite problem. New boots are a classic one, they give you blisters, but we usually warn people to try them first. The mistake I see most is that they don’t bring enough water. They think the cold means they won’t be thirsty, and then they feel ill by lunchtime.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: What is your best memory?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: A woman in her sixties, who had never climbed before. When she reached the top, she started crying with joy and hugged everybody. That’s much better than climbing alone at night, which I did once for a bet, or winning a race, which I did only for fun.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: What’s next for you?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: Next year I’m not going to stop working, even if my knees say otherwise, and I’m not opening a shop either. My wife suggested it, but I’d hate to stay inside. I’m going to train young guides. There aren’t enough of them, and I’d like to share what I know.

turns.speaker: clementine
turns.text: Do you have any final advice?

turns.speaker: gethin
turns.text: Respect the mountain, take enough water and turn back if you are not sure. The summit will always be there tomorrow.
